title: Using everyday devices to measure axial spondyloarthritis
official: Investigating computer vision and wearable-based measurement of disease metrics in axial spondyloarthritis
summary:
Background and study aims
Axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA) is a long-term condition that causes pain and stiffness in the spine. Doctors track how well the spine moves using a set of measurements called the BASMI, along with two other measures of physical function (the BASFI and ASPI). These are usually taken by a clinician in hospital and are infrequent due to limited resources. This study explores whether everyday devices — a smartphone, smartwatch and wireless earphones — and video recordings could take the same measurements at home. The aim is to find out whether these devices could one day let patients track their condition more often, including at home.

Who can participate?
Patients aged 18 years and over with axSpA who are attending a residential self-management course at the Royal National Hospital for Rheumatic Diseases and can follow instructions in English

What does the study involve?
Participants take part at three points during their 2-week course (days 1, 5 and 10). At each point they perform their usual axSpA movement and function assessments while wearing the devices and being video recorded. They also carry out a few short additional movements. The devices' motion sensors and the video are used to train computer models that estimate the measurements. The estimates are compared with the measurements taken by a clinician. Videos are converted into a simple 3D "skeleton", and the original recordings are deleted.

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
There is no direct benefit to participants, and the results will not affect their care. The risks are very low: the movements are the same as, or very similar to, those participants do anyway on the course, and the devices are ordinary consumer products worn as intended. There is a small chance of the pain or discomfort that axSpA movements can cause; participants can pause or skip any movement.

Where is the study run from?
The Royal National Hospital for Rheumatic Diseases at the Royal United Hospitals Bath NHS Foundation Trust, in collaboration with the University of Bath (UK)

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
August 2026 to February 2027

Who is funding the study?
The University of Bath as part of an EPSRC-funded PhD studentship (UK)

Who is the main contact?
Greg Knowles, grk24@bath.ac.uk

interventions.name: Commercially available consumer devices (iPhone, Apple Watch, AirPods Pro)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Adults aged 18 years and over
2. Diagnosed with axial spondyloarthritis
3. Attending a residential self-management programme at the Royal National Hospital for Rheumatic Diseases
4. Have the capacity for providing informed consent for participation
5. Sufficient communicative ability to participate in the research, and follow verbal or written instructions for the study procedures (must be able to communicate in English)
Exclusion criteria:
1. Those who would be unable to perform study procedures without psychological or physical discomfort, beyond that which they would experience on the self-management course
2. Previous spinal surgery
3. Significant degenerative spinal disease
4. Vertebral fractures
5. Known malignancy
6. Total spinal ankylosis
